stem: A provider prescribes an intravenous HUMULIN R (regular insulin) infusion for a hospitalized client. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Prepare the prescribed IV concentration in 0.9% sodium chloride and monitor blood glucose and potassium closely during the infusion.
options.B: Use the U-100 vial concentration directly in the IV line because dilution is required only for subcutaneous insulin administration.
options.C: Monitor blood glucose closely but omit potassium monitoring because intravenous regular insulin does not affect serum potassium.
options.D: Prepare the infusion in any concentration selected by the nurse because the label gives no concentration range for intravenous use.

rationale: HUMULIN R §2.2 permits IV administration only under medical supervision with close blood-glucose and potassium monitoring and specifies IV concentrations of 0.1 to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% sodium chloride. A follows these label requirements. B incorrectly uses the U-100 vial concentration directly, C omits potassium monitoring, and D ignores the labeled concentration range.
educational_objective: Prepare and monitor IV regular insulin according to the labeled concentration, diluent and safety-monitoring requirements.

source_original.stem: A provider prescribes an intravenous HUMULIN R (regular insulin) infusion for a hospitalized client. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Prepare the prescribed IV concentration in 0.9% sodium chloride and monitor blood glucose and potassium closely during the infusion.
options.B: Use the U-100 vial concentration directly in the IV line because dilution is required only for subcutaneous insulin administration.
options.C: Monitor blood glucose closely but omit potassium monitoring because intravenous regular insulin does not affect serum potassium.
options.D: Prepare the infusion in any concentration selected by the nurse because the label gives no concentration range for intravenous use.

source_original.rationale: Current HUMULIN R labeling permits IV administration only under medical supervision, requires close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium, and specifies IV concentrations of 0.1 to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% sodium chloride. Option A follows those labeled requirements. Option B incorrectly uses the U-100 vial concentration directly for IV infusion. Option C omits required potassium monitoring and falsely denies insulin-related hypokalemia risk. Option D ignores the labeled IV concentration range.
source_original.source_detail: DailyMed HUMULIN R — Dosage and Administration §2.2, Intravenous Administration: administer HUMULIN R intravenously ONLY under medical supervision with close monitoring of blood glucose and potassium; for IV use, use concentrations 0.1 unit/mL to 1 unit/mL in infusion systems containing 0.9% Sodium Chloride Injection. DailyMed HUMULIN R label updated 2025-05-27; §2.2 IV administration requirements live-rechecked 2026-08-15.
